runs.ladder-A: plain ladder, designer's pours restored, T0 20 M / T1 20 M / T2 50 M work
runs.ladder-P: ladder-A with --no-tracks-on In1.Cu,In2.Cu (planes kept free of signals)
runs.ladder-O: re-run with each board's own rules as T0 (robomezzi 0.178 mm, via 0.61/0.30; DronPi/EtherCAT via 0.6/0.4)
runs.human: the designer's own routing judged the same way
runs.ladder-W: ladder with a fourth tier T3 (0.4/0.2 via, experiment); E3 also with --layer-assign
runs.ladder-K: keep-power: supply AND ground nets stay at the board's own rules and are never narrowed (--no-neck-nets); relaxation spent on signals only
runs.ladder-K2: ladder-K with 200 M work at T2 (same result: more work does not help)
runs.ladder-G: keep-supply: supply rails stay strict, ground may relax (pours carry the ground current)
runs.ladder-M: graded power policy: signals take the whole ladder with power at the board's own rules (never narrowed); only if the board is still open do the power nets relax, one tier at a time (stage labels SIGNAL/POWER)
runs.closure-5: closure loop: relax only the nets in the way (power last), shove with track bending (D125), part moves, 5x-work round
runs.closure-5w: closure-5 with the designer's power widths (robomezzi human routing) as non-negotiable widths

findings: A board counts as routed only when KiCad reports 0 open AND the safety simulation (py/safety.py) does not FAIL; the router's 'routed N/N' alone is not enough.

Relaxing everything: robomezzi (ladder-O/P) and DronPi (ladder-O) close with 0 open and PASS the simulation (worst crosstalk 1.4 % / 0 % of swing) - but 216 / 111 of their compromises touch supply or ground copper.

Policy 'no relaxation on power nets' (ladder-K, --keep-power): zero compromises on power copper, but the boards no longer close at this budget: robomezzi 2 open, DronPi 35, E3 15, EtherCAT 13. More work (K2, 200 M) changes nothing.
Keeping supply rails strict but relaxing ground (ladder-G): robomezzi 1 open, DronPi 34, E3 14, EtherCAT 14; the rest are GND pour fragments plus pads of +3v3/1V8 that only route by necking down.
E3 best: 5 open (ladder-L, relaxes power) with a crosstalk WARN (10.8 % of swing); strict-power E3 (K) 15 open, WARN 16.7 %.
EtherCAT: the simulation rejects several routes (22 % and 42 % crosstalk of swing); the passing ones still have 9+ open QFN pins.
The designers' own layouts of all four judge clean (0 open): the placements are routable; the open pins are a router limit, not a rule limit.
Assumed, not datasheet: 40 ohm drivers, 1.5 ns edges, 5 pF loads, 50 mA per power pin of an IC/transistor, IPC-2221 outer 1 oz 10 C.
